answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called an ember, before it can post or attest. A single knoll checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 287 aliases therefore costs 380 bonds held for 18 days each, plus the kernel attestations those aliases can never earn. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
